analysis: This batch changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen38-mtp-forced-tools.md, lines 1-6) and a doc update to docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, new paragraph after base line 713 at head ~715-719). The prose says required/named tool_choice on Qwen 3.5-family checkpoints now accepts the inferred .qwen35 parser or .xmlFunction, and that the embedded-MTP Qwen3.8-27B build advertises forced tools via ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift. No executable code is in the supplied evidence. The implementing source change (ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift, the catalog/advertisement of tool_choice capability) was not supplied. So I cannot verify whether forced-tool acceptance for .qwen35 or the capability advertisement widens attack surface. Relevant boundaries: TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider contract) and TB-007 (inference engine). Nothing here touches the prefix cache (T-041), keys, attestation, authorization or encryption. The next pass should check the actual policy code if it appears in another batch. In particular, check that forced-tool enforcement still fails closed on parser mismatch and that the capability advertised to the coordinator matches real behavior. This is not a finding, only an unverified contract. No security regressions are identified in the supplied documentation changes.
